lost_facts.evidence: The agent's output_cap.py defines only `validate_max_output_bytes(max_output_bytes)` which raises a bare `ValueError('max_output_bytes must be at least 16 bytes, or 0 to disable capping (got {v})')` (transcript line ~3735 in the tool-call keystrokes at JSON idx 101) -- no `OutputCapError` class, no `.max_bytes` attribute, and different wording from the required `'max_bytes must be 0 or at least 16, got {value}'`. Grepping the whole transcript and the raw rollout JSON for 'OutputCapError' returns zero hits anywhere, confirming the agent never encountered that literal. The three remarks that name it -- g2.r1.l-floor-nikolai (OutputCapError, ValueError base, #cookbooks 2025-03-14), g2.r1.l-floor-konrad (.max_bytes attribute + exact message, #cookbooks 2025-03-17), and g2.r1.say26 (field_validator -> pydantic ValidationError verbatim, #incidents 2025-03-14) -- are all marked not-found by the pointer sheet, and direct greps for their distinctive phrases ('regex the traceback', 'hang the offending value', 'reads fine in a tracback', 'ValidationError comes back out carrying') return zero hits in the transcript. Root cause: the agent's Mattermost search used a fixed 5-term list (max_output_bytes/elided/output_cap/truncated_streams/error_truncated) that does not contain any of these remarks' distinctive words, and although #cookbooks was fully dumped to a local file, the agent only ever sed'd lines 668-750 and 691-705 of it (visible in tool calls at JSON idx 75/77/79) -- both remarks sit earlier in the file (2025-03-14/03-17, before the April/May clusters actually read). #incidents (holding say26) was never fetched at all -- it is not among the 7 channels the agent bulk-dumped (mzppa4bm=#code-review, tzfbbuxj=#cookbooks, yrz3eu98=#engineering, 386x6y65=#help, 93twxukt=#releases, mr6zzi1n=#pipeline, 94smn68j=#viewer; #general and #incidents are absent).

search_strategy: Wiki: exemplary -- searched BookStack /api/search for a handful of terms, correctly identified that comments carry the substance (the ticket explicitly warns about this), and fetched all 3 relevant pages whole via /api/pages/{id} including comments (steps 5-7), catching all 3 wiki-comment clues. Mail: also thorough -- IMAP TEXT search for the same keyword list found 2 threads directly, then the agent fetched a batch of message ids (106,108,115,124,129,136-142) around them and caught all 5 mail clues. Chat: the weak link. The agent built a Mattermost /posts/search script using a fixed 5-term keyword list (max_output_bytes, elided, output_cap, truncated_streams, error_truncated) which is the single biggest search step (24) and surfaced the great majority of found remarks in one shot, including all 4 herrings and both reversals. It then bulk-dumped 7 of the 9 channels to local files (step 24/51) but read only narrow sed line-ranges of each dump (step 27+) rather than the whole file, which is why several early-dated remarks in #cookbooks and #engineering were missed even though the raw text was sitting on disk. #general and #incidents were never fetched at all, silently losing every remark that lived only there (4 remarks total, including two of the three carriers of g2.r1.failure_behavior). Gitea issues were checked by title only and correctly judged irrelevant. No truncation or crashed helper scripts; the only friction was a malformed token file that self-corrected in one retry (line ~1910).
end_reason: Not applicable -- the run completed normally: pushed to Gitea main (commit 58bd02b, line 4878), Gitea Actions reported success for that commit (line 4949), and the deploy daemon picked up release 20260908220754-58bd02b with `current` pointing at it (line 5191/5221). provenance.pushed/ci_green/deployed are all 1 and g2.suite_ok is 1. reward 0.8889 reflects one lost fact (g2.r1.failure_behavior), not a run failure.
notable: line ~3735 (JSON idx 101): the agent invented a materially different exception (bare ValueError, different message, no .max_bytes) for the floor check, because it never read either remark naming OutputCapError -- a clean demonstration of the task's 'nobody states it, so a reasonable implementer guesses wrong' design.
line 2056: channel-id-to-name mapping recovered from the mmdump.py output confirms #general and #incidents (4 remarks total) were never fetched by any means -- not searched, not dumped.

lines 668-750/691-705 (JSON idx 75/77/79) and 1855-1885/2252-2310 (JSON idx 69/71/73): the agent's own sed ranges into #cookbooks and #engineering dumps only ever covered April-May/Dec clusters, systematically missing every March-dated remark in those two channels even though the full text was already on disk locally.

the grader's test_r1.py itself documents (in a comment) that it deliberately does NOT grade the OutputCapError constructor arity, only the exception identity/message/.max_bytes -- so this loss is a clean 'never saw the literal' miss, not an over-strict grader artifact.

line ~3898 (JSON tool output): the agent self-verified cap_text('x'*100,64) == 48+29+16 bytes with 36 dropped, i.e. it correctly re-derived the outside-the-budget marker arithmetic from first principles/found remarks even where specific fixture remarks (say18, l-bytes-gideon) were missed.
